title: He is risen, as he said — Psalm 16, the third day of Hosea and Jonah, and the firstfruits sheaf (Leviticus 23; Acts 2; 1 Corinthians 15)
summary:
It ain't new. The women come to the tomb at the end of the Sabbath and are told what he had told them:

*In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1)

*He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6)

*But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.* (Matthew 26:32)

David had written the rising a thousand years before, and Peter and Paul both said this was the verse:

*For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Psalm 16:10)

*He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Messiah (Christ), that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.* (Acts 2:31)

*Wherefore he saith also in another psalm, Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Acts 13:35)

The third day was Hosea's, spoken over the house that would be raised up, and Jonah's, which Yahusha (Jesus) took as his own sign:

*After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.* (Hosea 6:2)

*Now Yahuah (LORD) had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.* (Jonah 1:17)

*For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40)

And the morning itself was in the Torah's calendar. The sheaf of firstfruits is waved before Yahuah (the LORD) on the morrow after the Sabbath, in Passover week, and Paul calls the risen one by the sheaf's name:

*Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest:* (Leviticus 23:10)

*And he shall wave the sheaf before Yahuah (LORD), to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.* (Leviticus 23:11)

*But now is Messiah (Christ) risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.* (1 Corinthians 15:20)

*But every man in his own order: Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ’s) at his coming.* (1 Corinthians 15:23)

A firstfruits sheaf is the first of a harvest, waved so that the rest may be accepted. He rose on the day the sheaf was waved, first of them that slept, and the order Paul gives is the order of the harvest: he first, afterward those that are his at his coming. The rising is also the Father's word over the trial's verdict:

*And declared to be the Son of Elohim (God) with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:* (Romans 1:4)

The council said blasphemy. The empty tomb on the morning of the sheaf said Son of Elohim (God), with power.

3216.prose: The same morning from the women's side. The sabbath was past and they had *bought sweet spices* to anoint a body they took to be still in the grave. Matthew gives the hour, Mark gives the errand, and both have the same faithful women walking to the same tomb.
3216.phrase: had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him
3216.sentence: The women bought spices once the sabbath was past, so they came expecting a body and not a risen man.

3217.prose: Luke gives the same dawn. They came on the first day, *very early in the morning*, carrying spices they had made ready beforehand. Matthew's women and Luke's are the same faithful witnesses, walking to a tomb they expected to find shut with him inside it.
3217.phrase: very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre
3217.sentence: Luke sets the women at the tomb at first light on the first day of the week, carrying spices for the dead.

3218.prose: John names Mary Magdalene and says it was *yet dark*. Matthew has the dawn beginning to break. It is one morning seen at two moments, and in both she is among the first to come and the first to see the tomb opened.
3218.phrase: cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre
3218.sentence: John puts Mary Magdalene at the tomb in the last of the dark, the same morning Matthew sees beginning to dawn.

3219.prose: David wrote this a thousand years before the women came. *Not leave my soul in hell* is the promise, and the one called *thine Holy One* was not left, and his body did not see corruption. Peter and Paul both said this was the verse, and the women walk into it at the end of the sabbath.
3219.sentence: David's line is the promise the empty tomb keeps: his soul is not left and his flesh does not decay.

3220.prose: The psalm ends its cry with a promise to tell. After the sabbath the women are the first to carry the news, and what they carry is that he is risen. The vindication starts as a message passed to *my brethren*, long before it fills *the congregation*.
3220.phrase: I will declare thy name unto my brethren
3220.sentence: The one delivered says he will tell his brethren, and the telling begins with the women sent from the tomb.

3221.prose: Hosea spoke *in the third day* over the house that would be raised up, and the women come at the dawn of that third day. Yahusha (Jesus) lay through the days and the sabbath ended on the morning they came. What Hosea said over the scattered house, the empty tomb begins.
3221.phrase: After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up
3221.sentence: Hosea's third day is the day the women find the tomb empty, the raising the scattered house was promised.

3222.prose: Jonah was *three days and three nights* in the fish, and Yahusha (Jesus) took that as his own sign. The women come at the end of the sabbath, when those days are done. Yahuah (LORD) *had prepared* the fish, and the grave had its appointed time as well.
3222.phrase: Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights
3222.sentence: Jonah's three days and three nights are the sign Yahusha (Jesus) took, and the women come when they are finished.

3223.prose: Paul calls the risen one *the firstfruits of them that slept*. The women come on the morning after the sabbath in Passover week, the morning the sheaf was waved. He rose first, and the rest of the harvest follows in its order.
3223.phrase: risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept
3223.sentence: Paul names the risen Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits, the first of the harvest waved so the rest may be accepted.

3224.prose: Peter tells Yashar'el (Israel) that Elohim (God) *loosed the pains of death*, because the grave could not keep him. The women arrive to find it kept nothing. What Peter preaches is what they walk into on the morning after the sabbath, and he goes straight on to David's words in the psalm.
3224.phrase: having loosed the pains of death: because it was not possible that he should be holden of it
3224.sentence: Peter says death could not hold him, which is what the women find at the tomb.

3225.prose: Paul says the promise made to the fathers is *fulfilled the same unto us their children* by the raising of Yahusha (Jesus). The women at the tomb are the first to meet it. A few verses on, Paul goes to the same psalm Peter used, that the Holy One would not see corruption.
3225.phrase: Elohim (God) hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Yahusha (Jesus) again
3225.sentence: Paul says the promise to the fathers is kept to their children in the raising of Yahusha (Jesus).

5362.prose: The evening of the preparation is when the body is laid down, and the sabbath rests over it. David had written a thousand years before that the soul would not be left and the Holy One would not *see corruption*. The sabbath is the waiting, and the psalm is the promise under it.
5362.sentence: David's promise covers the hours between the burial at evening and the dawn after the sabbath.

5361.prose: That evening a rich man asked for the body, and Isaiah had said it: *with the rich in his death*. The man who had done *no violence* dies among the wicked and is laid in a rich man's grave, and it happens on the day before the sabbath.
5361.phrase: he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death
5361.sentence: Isaiah says where the body would be laid, and the burial on the preparation day is that grave.

5366.prose: The women see a young man in white and are afraid, and what he has for them is that the tomb is empty. David's line is the reason. The one called *thine Holy One* was not left, so there is nothing in the grave to see. The fear in the tomb answers a promise written long before.
5366.sentence: David's promise explains the empty tomb: the soul is not left and the body does not decay.

5367.prose: The women are afraid in the empty tomb, and the psalm says what comes after fear. The one delivered says he will tell *my brethren* and praise in *the congregation*. The faithful women are sent out of the tomb with news to carry, and the telling begins with them.
5367.phrase: I will declare thy name unto my brethren
5367.sentence: After the deliverance comes the telling to his brethren, and the women carry the first word out of the tomb.
